title: Whole Turkey (frozen)

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Supplier warns of short delivery; no historical data on this risk, but plausible demand impact due to potential out-of-stocks. Noise-adjusted effect of supply risks on similar products is ~10% downside.

adjustment.analysis: No events, promotions, or price changes in target week. Baseline shows strong seasonal trend (44% 13-week growth), but target is 8 weeks post-last data—seasonal ramp may be plateauing. Supplier delivery warning introduces supply risk, lowering demand certainty. Past promotions show high noise; noise-adjusted lift is x1.0. No uplift signal from model. Downside risk from potential stockouts due to supply issue. Adjust median slightly down, widen downside spread.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 2.5 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 14.8 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-122% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
